My neighbor mentioned the two might not mix. Is it okay to keep taking ibuprofen with my blood thinner, or should I do something else for the pain?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I'm on daily warfarin for thromboembolism risk. My back has been hurting, so yesterday I started OTC ibuprofen, which helps. My neighbor mentioned a possible drug interaction. Is it okay to keep taking an NSAID alongside my anticoagulant, or should I switch analgesics?

checklist.text: Warns that combining ibuprofen (or NSAIDs generally) with warfarin raises bleeding risk — a serious, well-established interaction
Advises stopping the ibuprofen and/or contacting a doctor or pharmacist promptly before continuing it
Suggests acetaminophen/paracetamol as the usual safer over-the-counter alternative for the pain
Notes bleeding warning signs to watch for (e.g., unusual bruising, black/tarry stools, blood in urine, prolonged bleeding)

phrasings.lay-polished: My two-year-old spiked a fever of 104 tonight. She took some fever medicine an hour ago but she's still hot, and she seems limp and sleepy and doesn't want to drink anything. The pediatrician's office is closed until morning. Should we just wait it out overnight, or do something now?
phrasings.jargon-polished: My two-year-old spiked a 104 fever tonight. An antipyretic an hour ago hasn't brought it down, and she's lethargic and refusing fluids. The pediatrician's office is closed until morning. Should we observe overnight, or escalate now?
phrasings.lay-rough: my 2 year old spiked a fever of 104 tonight. she took some fever medicine a hour ago but shes still hot, an she seems limp an sleepy an dont want to drink nothin. the doctors office is closed till mornin.. shuld we just wait it out overnight or do somethin now

checklist.text: Treats lethargy/listlessness plus refusing fluids in a toddler as red flags needing urgent medical attention tonight, not waiting until morning
Directs to urgent evaluation now (ER or after-hours/nurse line; emergency services if unresponsive, seizing, or hard to rouse)
Notes the child's behavior and responsiveness matter more than the exact thermometer number
Mentions dehydration risk from refusing fluids

checklist.text: Identifies nerve damage from longstanding high blood sugar (diabetic neuropathy) as the likely explanation
Advises seeing their clinician for evaluation and discussing better glucose control, rather than self-managing

Advises prompt medical attention for any foot wound that isn't healing or looks infected

checklist.text: Treats sudden new floaters plus flashes as a possible retinal tear/detachment — urgent, not something to wait a month on
Advises a same-day or next-day dilated eye exam (eye specialist, or ER if none available)
Notes that absence of pain does not make it benign
Names signs meaning go immediately: a curtain/shadow over vision, vision loss, or a sudden worsening of floaters/flashes

phrasings.lay-polished: The doctor diagnosed me with pneumonia five days ago and gave me a ten-day course of antibiotics. I'm on day five now and honestly feel almost back to normal. Can I stop taking the pills early and save the rest for next time, or do I need to finish all of them?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I was diagnosed with pneumonia five days ago and prescribed a ten-day antibiotic course. I'm on day five and feel almost back to baseline. Can I discontinue early and keep the remainder on hand, or should I complete the full course?

checklist.text: Advises against stopping on their own — complete the course or check with the prescriber before changing anything
Warns stopping early risks the infection returning or being incompletely treated
Advises against saving leftover antibiotics for future self-treatment
Gives the reasoning (resistance and/or relapse risk), or notes duration decisions belong to the prescriber

phrasings.lay-polished: I owe about $12,000 across three credit cards. One charges 19% interest, one 22%, and one 26%. I can put an extra $400 a month toward them beyond the minimum payments. Which card should I pay down first, and does the order really matter?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I'm carrying about $12,000 in revolving balances across three credit cards at 19%, 22%, and 26% APR. I can allocate an extra $400 a month beyond the minimums. Which balance should I target first, and does the payoff order materially affect total interest?
phrasings.lay-rough: i owe abt 12000 across 3 credit cards. one charges 19 percent interest, one 22 an one 26. i can put a extra 400 a month toward them beyond the minimum payments.. wich card shuld i pay down first an does the order really matter

checklist.text: Recommends highest-rate-first (avalanche): target the 26% card first, then 22%, then 19% — this minimizes total interest
Mentions smallest-balance-first (snowball) as a legitimate motivation-based alternative
Says to keep paying minimums on all cards while targeting one
Advises not adding new charges to the cards while paying them down
Mentions balance-transfer offers or asking issuers for a lower rate as options, with their caveats (fees, promo windows)

phrasings.lay-polished: My car was totaled in an accident. The insurance company is offering $9,800 for it, but I still owe $13,000 on my car loan. Do I still have to pay the difference even though the car is gone? And is there anything I can do about the low offer?
phrasings.jargon-polished: My car was totaled. The insurer's actual cash value settlement is $9,800, but my loan payoff is $13,000. Am I still liable for the deficiency even though the vehicle is gone? And can I dispute the valuation?
phrasings.lay-rough: my car got totaled in a accident. the insurance company is offerin 9800 for it but i still owe 13000 on my car loan.. do i still have to pay the difference even though the car is gone, an is there anything i can do abt the low offer
phrasings.jargon-rough: my car got totaled. the insurers actual cash value settlement is 9800 but my loan payoff is 13000.. am i still liable for the deficiency even though the vehicle is gone, an can i dispute the valuation

checklist.text: States clearly that yes — the remaining loan balance is still owed; the debt doesn't disappear with the car
Notes the settlement goes to the lender (lienholder) first, and the borrower owes whatever remains
Advises checking for gap coverage (own policy or in the loan agreement) — it exists for exactly this situation
Notes the valuation can be disputed with comparable local listings or the policy's appraisal process
Advises continuing loan payments meanwhile to protect their credit

phrasings.lay-polished: I got a letter saying it's from the IRS. It says I owe $4,300 in taxes on money I made from gig work last year, and I can't pay that all at once. I'm worried it might also be some kind of scam. What should I do?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I received a notice stating it's from the IRS assessing $4,300 on unreported gig income from last year, and I can't pay in full. I'm also concerned it could be fraudulent. What should I do?

checklist.text: Advises verifying the notice is genuine (look up the notice number on irs.gov / call the official IRS number; real IRS starts by mail and never demands gift cards or wire transfers)
Warns not to ignore it — interest and penalties accrue and it won't go away
Mentions payment options for those who can't pay in full, e.g. an installment agreement/payment plan
Suggests checking the amount against their own records/1099s — assessments can be wrong and can be disputed

phrasings.lay-polished: I just inherited $25,000. I have a $6,000 emergency fund, a car loan at 6.5% with about $11,000 left, and my job's retirement plan matches contributions but I don't put in enough to get the full match. Should I invest the money or pay off the car loan?

I hold a $6,000 emergency fund, an auto loan at 6.5% APR with an $11,000 balance, and my employer's 401(k) matches contributions but I'm not contributing enough to capture the full match. Should I deploy the money into investments or retire the auto loan?
phrasings.lay-rough: i just inherited 25000. i got a 6000 emergency fund, a car loan at 6.5 percent w abt 11000 left, an my jobs retirement plan matches contributions but i dont put in enough to get the full match.. shuld i invest the money or pay off the car loan

checklist.text: Prioritizes capturing the full employer match — it's an immediate guaranteed return no investment beats
Frames paying the 6.5% loan as a guaranteed 6.5% return and compares it honestly against uncertain market returns
Recommends a concrete order/split rather than all-or-nothing (e.g., fix the match, then divide between loan payoff and investing; keep the emergency fund intact)
Cautions against putting the windfall into speculative bets (hot stocks, crypto, etc.)

phrasings.lay-polished: I took out a $500 payday loan two months ago and I've already rolled it over twice. Each time they charge another fee, and I'm now paying more in fees than I'm putting toward the loan itself. I get paid every two weeks but can never quite clear it. How do I get out of this?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I took a $500 payday loan two months ago and have rolled it over twice. Each renewal adds another finance charge, and my fees now exceed my principal reduction. I'm paid biweekly but can never fully retire the balance. How do I get out of this?

checklist.text: Names the rollover cycle as a debt trap with effectively triple-digit annualized cost — breaking the cycle is the priority, not another rollover
Mentions asking about an extended payment plan (required in many states) or state payday-lending protections
Suggests cheaper replacement credit or help: credit-union payday-alternative loan, small personal loan, or nonprofit credit counseling
Explains that any plan reducing principal beats rollovers, where payments vanish into fees

phrasings.lay-polished: I moved out of my apartment after three years and left it clean. My landlord kept my entire $1,800 security deposit, saying it was for repainting and general cleaning. That feels wrong to me. Is this normal, and what can I do to get my deposit back?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I vacated my unit after a three-year tenancy and left it clean. My landlord withheld my entire $1,800 security deposit, citing repainting and general cleaning. That seems improper. Is that permissible, and what remedies do I have to recover the deposit?

checklist.text: Explains normal wear and tear (including repainting after a multi-year tenancy, in most places) generally cannot be deducted from a deposit
Advises demanding an itemized statement of deductions in writing — many jurisdictions require one within a deadline
Mentions a written demand letter and then small claims court as the usual recourse
Notes rules/deadlines vary by state and that some allow extra (multiple) damages for bad-faith withholding — check local tenant resources

phrasings.lay-polished: I make $38,000 a year as a salaried office manager and I've been working about 60 hours a week. My boss says salaried employees never get overtime, no matter the hours. That doesn't sound right to me. Is he correct, and is there anything I can do?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I earn $38,000 as a salaried office manager and have been logging about 60 hours weekly. My employer claims salaried employees are categorically exempt from overtime. That doesn't sound right. Is that accurate, and what recourse do I have?
phrasings.lay-rough: i make 38000 a year as a salaried office manager an ive been workin abt 60 hours a week. my boss says salaried employees never get overtime no matter the hours. that dont sound right to me.. is he correct an is there anything i can do

checklist.text: Corrects the claim: being paid a salary alone doesn't eliminate overtime — exemption depends on job duties AND a salary threshold
Notes that at this salary and role they may well be overtime-eligible (non-exempt)
Advises keeping their own detailed record of hours worked
Mentions filing a wage claim with the Department of Labor or state labor agency (or consulting an employment attorney)
Notes retaliation for wage complaints is illegal, and to document everything

phrasings.lay-polished: A week after I told HR I was pregnant, I was let go in a 'restructuring' — but my duties were immediately posted as an open job. I had good performance reviews. Was this legal, and what should I do if I think it was because of the pregnancy?
phrasings.jargon-polished: A week after I disclosed my pregnancy to HR, I was terminated in a 'restructuring' — but my role was immediately reposted. My performance reviews were strong. Was this lawful, and what should I do if I believe it was pregnancy discrimination?
phrasings.lay-rough: a week after i told hr i was pregnant i got let go in a restructuring, but my duties got posted as a open job right away. i had good performance reviews.. was this legal an wat shuld i do if i think it was because of the pregnancy

checklist.text: States pregnancy discrimination is illegal even in at-will employment, and that the timing plus the reposted role are meaningful evidence
Advises preserving documentation now: reviews, emails, the job posting, a written timeline
Mentions filing an EEOC (or state agency) charge and that strict deadlines apply (typically 180/300 days)
Suggests consulting an employment lawyer (free consultations/contingency are common)

phrasings.lay-polished: A debt collector has been calling my workplace almost every day about a debt that belongs to my brother, not me. phrasings.jargon-polished: A collection agency has been calling my workplace almost daily about a debt that belongs to my brother, not me. They disclose details about the debt to my coworkers and insist I need to resolve it. Is this permissible, and how do I make it stop?
phrasings.lay-rough: a debt collector been callin my workplace almost every day abt a debt that belongs to my brother not me. they tell my coworkers details abt the debt an say i need to handle it. its embarrassin an im worried abt my job.. can they do this an how do i make it stop

checklist.text: Identifies this conduct as violating federal debt-collection law (FDCPA): harassment, discussing the debt with third parties, workplace calls
States clearly they are not responsible for a sibling's debt and should not pay or promise to pay it
Advises a written cease/limited-contact demand (including no workplace calls) and keeping a log of the calls
Mentions complaining to the CFPB or state attorney general, and that statutory damages/suing is possible for violations

phrasings.lay-polished: My heat hasn't worked for a month, so last week I reported my landlord to the city code office. Three days later he taped an eviction notice to my door. I've always paid rent on time. Can he actually evict me for complaining, and what should I do right now?
phrasings.jargon-polished: My heat has been out for a month, so last week I filed a code-enforcement complaint against my landlord. Three days later he served an eviction notice. My rent history is current. Is this retaliatory eviction actionable, and what should I do right now?
phrasings.lay-rough: my heat hasnt worked for a month so last week i reported my landlord to the city code office. 3 days later he taped a eviction notice to my door. ive always paid rent on time.. can he actually evict me for complainin an wat shuld i do right now

checklist.text: Explains many jurisdictions presume retaliation when eviction closely follows a code complaint — the timing is itself a defense
Clarifies a notice is not an eviction: only a court can evict; don't move out or panic, and never ignore court papers
Advises documenting everything: complaint date, the notice, photos of the heat problem, rent payment records
Directs to local legal aid or a tenant organization promptly, and notes response deadlines are short if a court case is filed

phrasings.lay-polished: I got a text saying my bank account was locked, and I clicked the link and typed in my username and password before realizing the website looked off. Nothing bad has happened yet as far as I can tell. What should I do now?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I got a smishing text claiming my bank account was locked, and I entered my credentials on the linked page before realizing the site was spoofed. No unauthorized activity is visible yet. What should I do now?
phrasings.lay-rough: i got a text sayin my bank account was locked an i clicked the link an typed in my username an password b4 realizin the website looked off. nothin bad happened yet as far as i can tell.. wat shuld i do now

substitutions: typed in my username and password

checklist.text: Change the bank password immediately (from a device believed clean) and anywhere that password is reused
Contact the bank through its official number or app — not the text — to flag the compromise and watch or freeze the account
Enable two-factor authentication on the account
Monitor statements and consider a fraud alert/credit freeze; treat follow-up calls or texts claiming to be the bank as suspect

phrasings.lay-polished: I found out my ex still knows the password to my main email account, and I think they've been reading my messages. I use that email for pretty much everything. What should I do to lock them out and make sure they can't get back in?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I found out my ex still knows the credentials to my primary email account, and I suspect they've been accessing my messages. That inbox anchors most of my accounts. How do I revoke their access and prevent re-entry?
phrasings.lay-rough: i found out my ex still knows the password to my main email account an i think theyve been readin my messages. i use that email for pretty much everything.. wat shuld i do to lock them out an make sure they cant get back in
phrasings.jargon-rough: i found out my ex still knows the credentials to my primary email account an i suspect theyve been accessin my messages. that inbox anchors most of my accounts.. how do i revoke their access an prevent re-entry

checklist.text: Change the password now to a strong unique one, and sign out all active sessions/devices
Check for persistence tricks: forwarding rules/filters, changed recovery email/phone, app passwords, connected third-party apps — remove anything unrecognized
Enable two-factor authentication
Notes this email anchors other accounts — review activity and consider rotating passwords on important linked accounts

phrasings.lay-polished: A message took over my computer screen saying all my files are locked and I have to pay $500 in bitcoin within 48 hours to get them back. I have some of my files backed up online from last month. Should I pay them? What do I do first?
phrasings.jargon-polished: A ransom note has taken over my screen saying my files are encrypted and demanding $500 in bitcoin within 48 hours for the decryption key. I have partial cloud backups from last month. Should I pay the ransom? What's the first move?
phrasings.lay-rough: a message took over my computer screen sayin all my files are locked an i have to pay 500 in bitcoin within 48 hours to get them back. i got some of my files backed up online from last month.. shuld i pay them, wat do i do first
phrasings.jargon-rough: a ransom note took over my screen sayin my files are encrypted an demandin 500 in bitcoin within 48 hours for the decryption key. i got partial cloud backups from last month.. shuld i pay the ransom, wats the first move

checklist.text: Advises against paying — no guarantee of recovery, and it funds/marks them for repeat targeting
Disconnect the machine from the internet/network right away to limit spread
Lays out the recovery path: clean or wipe/reinstall the machine, then restore from the existing backups
Mentions reporting (e.g., FBI IC3 or local equivalent) and/or checking free decryptor resources like No More Ransom
Cautions against 'tech support' phone numbers or tools promoted by the ransom note or found in panicked searching

phrasings.lay-polished: I'm traveling and the only internet I have is the free hotel wifi. I need to log into my bank account tonight to pay a bill. Is that safe on hotel wifi, or is there a safer way I should do it?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I'm traveling with only the hotel's open wifi available. I need to log into online banking tonight to pay a bill. Is that safe on an open network, or is there a lower-risk alternative?
phrasings.lay-rough: im travelin an the only internet i got is the free hotel wifi. i need to log into my bank account tonight to pay a bill.. is that safe on hotel wifi or is there a safer way i shuld do it
phrasings.jargon-rough: im travelin w only the hotels open wifi available. i need to log into online banking tonight to pay a bill.. is that safe on a open network or is there a lower-risk alternative

checklist.text: Notes banking sites/apps encrypt the connection (HTTPS/TLS), which protects session content even on open wifi — the risk is real but often overstated
Names the actual risks: look-alike/evil-twin networks and fake login/captive portals capturing what you type
Recommends the safer route: use cellular data or the phone as a hotspot (and/or the bank's official app or a reputable VPN)
Practical hygiene: verify the exact network name with staff, avoid entering details into popups/portals, log out when done

phrasings.lay-polished: I'm selling my old smartphone to a stranger online. I did a factory reset from the settings menu. Is that enough to make sure they can't get at my photos, passwords, and banking apps, or do I need to do something more?
phrasings.jargon-polished: I'm selling my old smartphone to a stranger online. I performed a factory reset from settings. Is that sufficient to prevent recovery of my photos, credentials, and banking apps, or are additional steps needed?
phrasings.lay-rough: im sellin my old smartphone to a stranger online. i did a factory reset from the settings menu.. is that enough to make sure they cant get at my photos, passwords an bankin apps or do i need to do somethin more
phrasings.jargon-rough: im sellin my old smartphone to a stranger online. i performed a factory reset from settings.. is that sufficient to prevent recovery of my photos, credentials an bankin apps or are additional steps needed

checklist.text: Explains modern phones encrypt storage, so a completed factory reset makes personal data practically unrecoverable — reset is broadly sufficient
Before handing it over: sign out of the platform account and disable activation/find-my locks (otherwise it stays tied to the seller and useless to the buyer)
Remove the SIM card and any SD card — SD cards are not reliably wiped by a reset
Suggests confirming the wipe finished (setup/welcome screen) and the device no longer appears in their account's device list
